core_obligations: Propose the quasi-inverse (proof lines 23113-23121): as in the integral case, send the descent datum (F, phi) to G = Equalizer(f_*F => f_{1,*}F_1) and note that it suffices to show that f^{-1}G -> F is an isomorphism; this may be checked locally, so assume Y affine.

Reduce by a finite cover (proof lines 23122-23131): using the domination lemma find a finite surjective Z -> Y with an open covering Z = union W_i such that W_i -> Y factors through X; by the after-base-change checking lemma it suffices to prove the statement after replacing Y by Z and by Z x_Y Z and f by its base change.

Conclude by sections (proof lines 23132-23143): after this reduction f has sections Zariski locally, and since the problem is local on Y one reduces to the case of a morphism with a section, which is the sections lemma.
proof_roadmap: Write the quasi-inverse as the equalizer of the two pushforwards and reduce to f^{-1}G = F locally on Y.
Dominate the fppf cover by a finite surjective morphism with a Zariski local factorisation, and use the base-change checking lemma to pass to it.
In the presence of local sections apply the sections lemma.
difficulty_reason: The lemma extends etale descent from surjective integral morphisms to surjective flat locally finitely presented morphisms (statement lines 23099-23110). The proof (proof lines 23112-23143) reuses the equalizer form of the quasi-inverse, reduces by a finite surjective cover dominating the fppf cover with a Zariski local factorisation, applies the base-change checking lemma to pass to that cover and to its square, and finishes with the sections case. H2: one reduction through a finite cover plus one localisation, written out.
